paper_title: ASyMOB Algebraic Symbolic Mathematical Operations Benchmark
caption: belowskip=0pt : Effect of equivalence-type perturbations. Note the substantial drop in success rate for most models, even when performance on the seed set is high.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the success rates of various models on different equivalence-type perturbations, comparing their performance across multiple categories. The horizontal axis lists 15 models, including Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code), Gemini 2.5 Flash (No Code), and others, while the vertical axis represents the success rate percentage, ranging from 0 to 100 in intervals of 20. Each model is associated with a group of five bars, colored in different shades of blue according to the legend, representing 'Seed', 'Equivalence-One-Easy', 'Equivalence-One-Hard', 'Equivalence-All-Easy', and 'Equivalence-All-Hard'. The 'Seed' category has the highest success rate for most models, with values close to or at 100%, while the other categories exhibit varying degrees of success, with 'Equivalence-All-Hard' generally having the lowest success rates, often below 20%. The bars within each group are not stacked, and their heights vary significantly across models and categories. Some models, such as Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code) and o4-mini (Code), consistently show high success rates across the different categories, whereas others, like DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, exhibit a substantial drop in success rate for the 'Equivalence-All-Hard' category. The models are listed in a specific order, but there is no clear indication of sorting by success rate or alphabetical order. Overall, the chart provides a visual representation of how different models perform under various equivalence-type perturbations, highlighting the differences in their robustness.
